Purchasing with Purpose: Procurement on Sponsored Projects

Hello Morgan State University Faculty & Staff, In this module, we will review key processes for procurement of goods and services on sponsored projects at Morgan State University. Topics include purchasing supplies with a University purchasing card, the requisition process in Banner, procurement of services, invoice processing through Accounts Payable, and more. Please note that the processes detailed in this module are specific to grant-funded activities. Some of the information may also be relevant to state-funded actions; however, policy and procedural differences may apply. We strive to continuously review these lessons to provide up-to-date guidance on Morgan’s sponsored project processes. ## Uniform Guidance: Subpart E
UG: Cost Accounting Standards (CAS) Basics
Subpart E of the Uniform Guidance establishes the federal cost principles used to determine whether costs may be charged to a federal award. For procurement activity, Subpart E helps answer a basic but important question: “Can this purchase appropriately be paid for with grant funds?” These principles require costs to be allowable , allocable to the award, reasonable for the work being performed, and treated consistently with institutional policies and accounting practices. 2 CFR 200.403 , Factors Affecting Allowability of Costs, provides the general standards that must be met before a cost can be charged to a federal award.
Allowability
Allowability asks whether a cost is permitted under the award, federal regulations, sponsor terms, and institutional policy. In procurement, this means the item or service must be necessary for the project and not specifically prohibited, such as entertainment costs, food/catering, or purchases outside the award’s approved purpose.
Allocability
Allocability asks whether the cost benefits the specific project being charged. A purchase should be assigned to a federal award only when that award actually receives the benefit, and if multiple projects benefit, the cost should be distributed in a reasonable and documented way. Please Note: End-of-period spending is highly scrutinized because purchases made near the award end date must clearly benefit the project during the remaining period of performance and cannot simply be used to spend down available funds.
Reasonableness
Reasonableness asks whether a prudent person would consider the purchase appropriate under the circumstances. This includes considering the price, timing, quantity, necessity, and whether the purchase reflects sound business judgment rather than convenience or personal preference.
Consistency
Consistency means costs must be treated the same way across the institution when similar circumstances exist. For example, if Morgan normally treats a certain type of cost as an indirect administrative expense (such as administrative employee salaries), it generally should not be charged directly to a grant unless the award circumstances clearly justify that treatment.

Procurement Types
Competition and Supporting Docs
Procurement requirements vary based on the total cost of the purchase. As the dollar value increases, additional supporting documentation, review, and competition may be required to ensure the purchase is properly justified, fairly competed, and compliant with MSU and State of Maryland procurement requirements. The section below outlines each procurement level, including the required documentation and level of competition needed before a purchase can move forward.
$0 - $5,000
The preferred method of procurement at this level is to utilize a MSU Purchasing Card (P-Card). If you do not have a p-card, and believe one is necessary for the success of your project, then contact the Purchase Card Office at pcard@morgan.edu. No formal competition required (1 quote only). Cost should be reasonable and allocable under your project's Notice of Award. Ensure IT purchases (laptops, desktops, etc.) meet the minimum requirements established by Morgan's Division of Information Technology.
$5,001 - $25,000
Competition is required. A minimum of three vendors must be consulted. Quotes may be informal (email, written, cart screenshot, or verbal with documentation). Award is generally granted to the vendor that provides the lowest price and meets the technical requirements of the scope of work (Lowest Price Technically Acceptable, LPTA). If lowest price is not selected, justification must be provided.
$25,001 - $100,000
Competition is required. A minimum of three vendors must be consulted. Typically procured via Request for Quotation (RFQ). The initiator must provide a Performance Work Statement (PWS) to establish the scope of the procurement. Procurement will post the RFQ and collect vendor submissions. After a set time, the proposals will be reviewed by Procurement and the established review committee (typically comprising of the initiator and other office staff). Proposals will be graded on their technical approach, management approach, and past performance. Evaluation of proposals is typically based on price and responsiveness. After the RFQ is posted the initiator should not contact the vendors directly. All questions should be relayed through the assigned Procurement technician.
$100,000 +
Please Note : For procurements of this size, please contact the Procurement department directly at services.procurement@morgan.edu as early as possible. Procurement Process Overview for 100k+ procurements PWS and RFP designed in partnership between initiator and Procurement team RFP is posted online through eMMA to solicit proposals Procurement team works with initiator to assemble proposal review committee Proposal review committee assess technical proposals on (1) technical approach (2) management approach (3) past performance Procurement invites qualified vendors for oral presentation Committee provides review on oral presentations A determination is then made on which vendor to select. Utilizing Preferred Vendors
Maryland’s procurement framework emphasizes the use of certified small, minority, veteran-owned, and other socioeconomic vendors where appropriate. Under State of Maryland Executive Order 01.01.2024.38 , procurement officers are directed to consider minority vendors when market research identifies two or more certified businesses capable of performing the work or providing the needed goods or services. Procurement's MBE Liaison can assist with identifying a certified firm to meet your procurement needs.
Minority Business Enterprise (MBE)
An MBE is a business certified through Maryland’s MBE Program as being owned and controlled by individuals who meet the program’s eligibility requirements, including minority status, ownership, control, business size, and personal net worth standards. Maryland’s MBE Program is intended to increase opportunities for minority- and women-owned businesses to participate in State contracting, either as prime contractors or subcontractors. Morgan's Goal: 29% of total institutional procurements.
Small Business Reserve (SBR)
The SBR Program is Maryland’s small business set-aside program. When a procurement is designated as SBR, only certified small businesses may compete for that opportunity, helping ensure that small businesses have a fair chance to participate in State procurement. Morgan's Goal: 15% of total institutional procurements.
Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise (VSBE)
A VSBE is a certified veteran-owned small business. Maryland’s VSBE Program creates contracting opportunities on State-funded procurements for qualified veteran-owned small businesses, and designated agencies and departments are directed to spend at least 3% of the dollar value of their procurement contracts with certified VSBE firms. Morgan's Goal: 3% of total institutional procurements.
Woman-Owned Businesses
A woman-owned business is generally a business owned, operated, and controlled by one or more women. In Maryland procurement, women-owned businesses may seek certification through applicable programs, including the MBE Program, where certified women-owned firms can count toward MBE participation goals if they meet the program’s requirements. Morgan's Goal: 1% of total institutional procurements.

## Tax Exempt Purchasing
Morgan State University: Tax Exempt Purchasing
Morgan State University, under the umbrella of the State of Maryland, maintains tax-exempt status for procuring goods and services. There are limited exceptions to this policy including hotel/lodging taxes and car rental tax fees assessed while on university-approved travel. All purchases made in Maryland using the MSU Purchasing Card (P-Card) outside of these limited exceptions should be tax free. For accidental tax charges the cardholder must work with the vendor to receive a refund.

## MSU: Subawards vs. Subcontracts
What Is a Subaward?
A subaward typically occurs when a primary grantee or institution receives federal funding and then further distributes a portion of those funds to a collaborating entity, often a subrecipient, to perform specific project-related tasks or activities. Subawards are usually utilized when the collaborating institution has a significant role in the project's design, conduct, or outcomes and they are responsible for their own compliance with federal regulations. In contrast, a subcontract is a contractual arrangement where a portion of the federal grant is allocated to a third-party organization or entity to provide specific goods or services related to the research project. Subcontracts are typically used when the collaborating entity is rendering specialized services and operates under the direct oversight of the primary grantee, who maintains control over the research direction and compliance obligations.
A subaward ( 2CFR200.331 ) is issued when a portion of a sponsored project is carried out by another organization that is acting as a subrecipient . In this arrangement, the external entity is responsible for performing a substantive portion of the programmatic work and contributes to overall project objectives. A subcontract (a.k.a. a contractor/vendor agreement ) is used when an external entity is engaged to provide goods and services that support a sponsored project, but does not take part in the programmatic direction or intellectual leadership of the work. The distinction between subawardee and subcontractor should be made prior to proposal submission. Any new subawards created during the performance period of the prime award will require sponsor approval.

Purchasing Supplies on Sponsored Projects
Supplies ( 2CFR200.453 ) are commonly needed to support the day-to-day work of a sponsored project. Supply, and other procurement, orders must be delivered to MSU main campus or an MSU-owned satellite location (such as MSU PEARL). What is a Micro-Purchase?
A micro-purchase is a low-dollar procurement of supplies or services that falls at or below Morgan State University’s micro-purchase threshold of $5,000 per transaction . The current federal micro-purchase threshold under FAR 2.101 is generally $15,000 , and 2 CFR 200.320 allows recipients to use lower institutional thresholds. Morgan applies a more restrictive institutional limit of $5,000 , so MSU users must follow the lower threshold. 2 CFR 200.320 states that micro-purchases may be awarded without soliciting competitive price or rate quotations if the recipient considers the price reasonable and maintains documentation supporting that conclusion.

Required Documentation
Whether the purchase is made by p-card or requisition, your files should include enough documentation to support the business purpose, project benefit, and allowability of the expense. Preferred Vendors
Before purchasing supplies, check whether the item is available through: Existing State contracts MSU preferred vendors MBE, SBE, VSBE, or other certified vendor options, when applicable Using established contracts or preferred vendors can improve compliance, reduce processing time, and support institutional procurement goals.
Sponsor-Specific restrictions
Always check sponsor-specific guidance before purchasing supplies. Examples include: NIH Grants Policy Statement (NIH GPS) NSF Proposal & Award Policies & Procedures Guide (NSF PAPPG) Award terms and conditions Sponsor prior approval requirements Restrictions in the approved budget or Notice of Award Some sponsors may restrict certain types of purchases, require prior approval, or expect additional documentation for items that appear unusual, high-risk, or not clearly tied to the project scope.
Technology Procurements
Technology-related purchases may require additional review before purchase. This may include: Computers, tablets, software, cloud-based tools, data storage, etc. Before purchasing technology, review Morgan's IT minimum hardware requirements to ensure they meet the product specifications necessary to link with Morgan's domain and IT support. Submitting your completed State of Maryland Transaction Log for review is the final step of your monthly p-card reconciliation duties. The MSU P-Card Office will review your documents for accuracy and reach out for any additionally required information.
Enter Transactions As They Occur
It is best practice to enter transactions on your log as they occur. This helps to ensure your Banner reconciliation goes smoothly and reduces the risk of being unable to complete the log in a time for the monthly submission deadline (15th of the month).

Transaction Details Part 1
The transaction details portion of the log has 7 columns to complete for each transaction. Starting from the left: Order Date This should match the "Transaction Date" for the purchase on your US Bank Statement. Vendor Name Purchase/Refund Amount A refund amount will be entered with a minus (-) sign in front of the dollar cost. Also, please contact the vendor to receive some form of confirmation of the refund amount (invoice/receipt, email, etc.)
Transaction Details Part 2
Sales Tax (if any) Sales tax charges should not be assessed on purchases using your State of Maryland purchasing card. If you are charged sales tax it is your responsibility to work with the vendor to have the tax charge remitted to your card. Exceptions to this rule include hotel/lodging and flight/train travel expenses. Description of Purchase The description does not need to be highly detailed (product specs, serial number, etc), but should be detailed enough to clearly describe the item/service rendered. If the cost is travel-related, you must note the traveler name and the associated travel authorization number in this line as well. Index/Budget Here you enter the six-digit index code assigned to the project/budget funding the transaction. This information, along with the account information, should match your entries during your Banner reconciliation on the 8th of the month. Account The correct account code to enter here will be based on the type of transaction. A list of Banner account codes is included in this module for your reference. If you are unsure which account code to assign you should reach out to your departmental budget officer or directly to pcardreconciliation@morgan.edu.
Verify Log Accuracy
At the end of the month you should review your US Bank Statement and verify that all monthly charges are accurately noted in your transaction log. Check the "Statement Total" on your US Bank statement and ensure it matches your "Log Total" on the State of Maryland Transaction Log.

Split Purchasing
Split Purchasing refers to the act of dividing a single transaction into several smaller transactions in order to circumvent increased Procurement oversight. Instead of splitting the purchase, the faculty/staff member must go through the Procurement process via requisition/purchase order. Repeated offenses will result in card termination. Example : You receive a quote for lab supplies that totals $6,000. In order to bypass the $5,000 purchase limit restriction, you ask the vendor to provide two quotes for $3,000 each in order to process payment with your card.
Charge Denial reasons
Maximum Purchase Limit Met: Your purchasing card has a single purchase limit referenced in your P-Card Office documentation. Any expense greater than that would need to either be sourced from multiple vendors or go through the procurement process via requisition/purchase order. Additionally, your card has a monthly purchasing limit set by the P-Card Office on a case-by-case basis. This amount can range up to $50,000 per month. Any threshold greater than $50,000 would require approval from the State of Maryland General Accounting Division (GAD). Fraud Protection: US Bank maintains certain protocols to help reduce the incidents of fraudulent p-card purchases. For example, if you haven't used your card for an extended period of time, then attempt to make a large purchase, US Bank may stop payment processing. In this case, you can call US BANK customer service at the number on your purchasing card to ask that the stop payment be lifted. MCC Group Block: The State and University prohibit certain Merchant Category Code (MCC) groups from purchasing card use. The Morgan State P-Card Office does not have the authority to override state blocks on MCC groups. For example, Orbitz.com is coded as an airline site (airline tickets being a banned card expense) and may not be an available travel resource.

## Equipment: Procurement Best Practices
Equipment Procurement on Sponsored Awards
Equipment purchases require additional planning before the purchase is submitted. For grant purposes, equipment generally means a single item with an acquisition cost of $5,000 or more and a useful life of more than one year . Equipment is excluded from the Modified Total Direct Cost (MTDC) base, meaning indirect costs are not charged on equipment purchases .
Additional Equipment Considerations
Equipment procurements must consider more than just the purchase price. Important factors may include title ownership, related costs, how the asset will be tagged and tracked, and whether the proposed location has the necessary facilities to support its use.

Facility Needs
Before purchasing equipment, the PI and department should confirm that the University has the space, utilities, and long-term support needed to use it successfully. This includes determining whether the equipment will fit in the intended location, whether alternate space is needed, and whether the location can support required utilities such as electrical, water, cooling, ventilation, or other installation needs. Any required space considerations should be addressed during the pre-award/proposal development phase . If space is needed, contact Morgan's Facilities, Design and Construction Management (FDCM) team early to confirm whether the project’s space needs can be met upon receipt of the Notice of Award.
Total Cost of Ownership
Departments should also consider the full cost of ownership, not just the purchase price. This may include delivery, installation, service agreements, calibration, maintenance, repairs, supplies, software, warranties, and any training needed for MSU faculty or staff to properly operate the equipment.
Equipment Title
Unless the sponsor or award terms state otherwise, title to equipment acquired under a federal award generally vests with the recipient or subrecipient, subject to federal requirements. Federally funded equipment must be used for the project for which it was acquired as long as it is needed. During that time, it should also be made available for use on other federally supported projects or programs, as long as that use does not interfere with the original project. First preference should be given to other projects supported by the same federal agency that funded the equipment. These requirements are outlined in 2 CFR § 200.313(c) .
Asset Tagging
Once equipment is purchased, it must be tagged through MSU Property Control . Tagging supports institutional asset tracking, helps Morgan maintain accurate property records, and allows for appropriate depreciation or amortization of MSU-owned assets. For federally funded equipment, Uniform Guidance also requires property records, physical inventory, safeguards against loss or damage, and adequate maintenance procedures. These requirements are outlined in 2 CFR § 200.313(d) .

## Non-Travel Reimbursement
Non-Travel Reimbursements
A non-travel reimbursement is used when an employee pays for allowable, non-travel expenses out of pocket, such as project supplies, and needs to be reimbursed by the University. This process should be used only when the purchase is appropriate for reimbursement and allowable on the funding source. Original receipts of the costs outlined in the form should be included when submitting your request. For food related costs you must include a list of attendees for the event.
